page: Amazon Web Services g4dn.8xlarge is an accelerated computing instance operating on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor. Hardware resources include an Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, providing 16 physical cores and 32 dedicated vCPUs with hyperthreading enabled. The system includes 128 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Hardware support includes AVX-512 vector extensions with VNNI, AES cryptographic acceleration, and 35 MB of L3 cache.

Hardware acceleration is anchored by a single NVIDIA T4 GPU based on the Turing architecture, offering 16 GB of video memory. In synthetic LLM inference benchmarks, this configuration achieves top-tier results in prompt processing and token generation for small (135M) and medium (7B) parameter models. However, throughput drops significantly when processing 70B parameter models due to the memory constraints of a single 16 GB frame buffer. CPU benchmarks place single-core operations in lower percentiles across stress-ng and Geekbench tests, while multi-core compute registers around median values.

The server incorporates bundled high-speed I/O components, featuring 900 GB of local NVMe SSD storage alongside a 50 Gbps baseline network interface. This combination eliminates the need for separate network-attached scratch disks during heavy data staging. From a cost efficiency perspective, bundling a mainstream accelerator with broad system memory and local NVMe storage provides strong resource density without requiring full enterprise training GPUs. The instance is suited for deep learning inference, video transcoding, distributed ETL pipelines, and graphics-intensive virtual workstation environments.
description: Amazon Web Services g4dn.8xlarge is an accelerated computing instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture, tailored for machine learning inference and graphics workloads. The configuration includes 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores via an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor at 2.5 GHz, paired with 128 GB of DDR4 system memory. Hardware acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA T4 GPU with 16 GB of Turing-generation VRAM. In addition, the instance bundles a dedicated 900 GB local NVMe SSD and provides a 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark evaluations highlight top-tier performance for small and medium language model prompt processing and inference generation, whereas CPU single-core operations remain in the lower tier and multi-core processing delivers average scores. With balanced memory and compute resources relative to its single accelerator, this instance fits machine learning inference pipelines, video transcoding, remote workstation graphics, and data ingestion tasks.
